name: RapidRAW
author: Timon Käch
summary: A beautiful, non-destructive, and GPU-accelerated RAW image editor built with performance in mind.
description:
RapidRAW is a modern, high-performance alternative to Adobe Lightroom®. It delivers a simple, beautiful editing experience in a lightweight package (under 20MB) for Windows, macOS, and Linux.

RapidRAW is for photographers who love to edit their photos in a clean, fast, and simple workflow. It prioritizes speed, a beautiful user interface, and powerful tools that let you achieve your creative color vision quickly.

It is not for users who seek absolute, perfect color accuracy. While the results are great for most purposes, the focus is on a fluid, creative process rather than perfect color precision.

RapidRAW is still in active development and isn't yet as polished as mature tools like Darktable, RawTherapee, or Adobe Lightroom®. Right now, the focus is on building a fast, enjoyable core editing experience. You may encounter bugs - if you do, please report them so I can fix them :) Your feedback really helps!

versions.release_notes:
I'm really excited to share this release, as it changes how every photo in RapidRAW looks. At its heart is Furka, a new rendering engine that reworks how RapidRAW turns a RAW file into a photo, from demosaicing all the way to the tone sliders. Your photos get cleaner fine detail, tone sliders that feel natural, and much more room to bring back bright skies and dark shadows. Next to it comes RapidRes, a 2x AI upscaler trained on RapidRAW's own RAW pipeline, which adds real detail to your photos. On top of that, you can now dock the filmstrip into the side panels, give each of your cameras its own default look, rotate a crop just by dragging around the frame, and enjoy many more improvements across the whole app.
New Features
Furka Rendering Engine
Furka is RapidRAW's new rendering engine. RAW files are now demosaiced on the GPU with RCD for Bayer sensors and Markesteijn for Fujifilm X-Trans, which removes most of the false color, maze patterns and moiré in fine detail. Highlights, Shadows, Whites, Blacks, Clarity and Structure were rebuilt on a new, edge-aware base, so they no longer create halos around mountains, trees and buildings. Highlight and shadow recovery are much stronger, Contrast now works around each photo's own midtones, sharpening is halo-free and the color grading wheels now work in OKLab.
You can read everything about Furka, with lots of comparisons, in the blog post: Introducing the Furka Rendering Engine
furka-blog-title
RapidRes AI Super Resolution
RapidRes is a new 2x AI upscaler that sits right next to AI Denoise in the Details panel. It is fine-tuned on RapidRAW's own Bayer and X-Trans pipeline, so it adds real detail without the plastic look of generic upscalers. A Detail slider controls how much fine detail it adds, and it works together with AI Denoise. Like AI Denoise, it is fully non-destructive and cached, so it only needs to run once per photo.
You can read more about how RapidRes was made, with comparisons, in the blog post: Introducing RapidRes
image
Docked Filmstrip
The filmstrip can now be docked into the left or right side panel as a vertical grid. This gives you much more room to see your photos on wide screens. The docked filmstrip has its own header, a quick filter, a toggle to show file names, and you can change the thumbnail size with Ctrl + mouse wheel.
Dragging panels between the side panels was also reworked. You can now drop a panel at the top or bottom of a side to split it, with a live preview of where it will land.
image
Default Adjustments
You can now choose what unedited photos start with in the new Default Adjustments settings.
- Default Preset: Pick a preset that is applied to every unedited photo. Masks, crops and transforms are skipped, since they only fit the photo they were made on.
- Per-Camera Defaults: Give photos from specific cameras their own preset. You can also right-click a preset while editing a photo and set it as the default for that camera.
- Automatic Lens Correction: Turn on lens correction for all photos, using the lens profile found in each photo's metadata.
- RAW Only: By default, the defaults only apply to RAW files, as JPEGs from your camera are usually already processed. You can turn this on for other files too.
- Slider Reset: Choose whether double-clicking a slider resets it to your default or to the neutral value.
image
Better Generative Fill & Cloud Inpainting
Generative fill now blends much better into the photo. Fills use a hard mask with a soft blend at the edge, and cloud inpainting sends more of the surrounding image at up to 2048 px and matches the tone and grain of your photo. The feather sliders are gone, as they are no longer needed.
image
With RapidRAW Cloud, you can remove objects, fill in empty areas and replace parts of your photo with high-quality AI, right inside RapidRAW. No powerful GPU or extra setup is needed if you don't want to self-host via ComfyUI.
RapidRAW is free and open source, and I work on it in my free time. Subscribing to RapidRAW Cloud is also the best way to support its development and keep new updates like this one coming. Thank you to everyone who already does!
Rotate Crop By Dragging
In crop mode, you can now rotate the image by dragging anywhere around the crop frame or outside the image. The cursor turns into a curved arrow that faces your pointer. Hold Shift or Alt while rotating for fine adjustments. The crop handles also have bigger hit areas now, which makes them easier to grab, especially on touch screens.
image
Library Improvements
- Six Thumbnail Sizes: The library now has six thumbnail sizes instead of three.
- Natural Sorting: File names are now sorted in natural number order, so frame_2 comes before frame_10.
- Camera Make & Model: The metadata panel now shows the camera make next to the model.
Core Improvements
- Smooth Zooming While Loading: RAW files are now decoded on their own GPU queue, so zooming and panning stay smooth while a photo is loading.
- Smaller AI Cache: The AI Denoise and RapidRes cache now takes about a third of the space. Old cache files still work. Both cache limits were raised to 25 GB.
- Metadata in JPEG XL & TIFF: JPEG XL exports now keep the RAW EXIF and XMP metadata, and the metadata export options are now shown for JPEG XL and TIFF.
- Exporting With AI: Exporting the open photo now waits for RapidRes and AI Denoise to finish, so they are always included.
- Virtual Copy Exports: Exported virtual copies are now numbered one after another.
- Copy & Paste: Motion Blur is now included when you copy and paste adjustments.
- Embedded Preview Notice: If a RAW file can't be decoded and RapidRAW falls back to the camera's embedded JPEG, a message now tells you, so its lower quality isn't mistaken for RapidRAW's processing.
- Opening From Your OS: Opening a photo from your file manager now loads its folder into the filmstrip without adding it to your library folders.
- AI Masks on Linux: Fixed AI sky, subject, face and text masks on Linux systems that use a decimal comma.
- Renaming: Fixed renames that left sidecar files behind, and renames that only change upper and lower case now work.
- Mask Drawing: Fixed the mask overlay jumping while drawing at high zoom.
- Stability & Bug Fixes: Resolved various issues and refined overall application performance.
Note for Upgrading Users
This is a significant rendering update. The Furka engine changes how every photo is rendered, so your existing edits will look different after updating. If you are in the middle of a project, I recommend finishing and exporting it before you upgrade.
- Color Grading: The color wheels now work in OKLab and will look the most different. Edits that use color grading will likely need to be adjusted again.
- Tone Sliders: Highlights, Shadows, Whites, Blacks, Contrast, Clarity and Structure were rebuilt and have different strengths. Edits with strong values may need a small touch-up.
- Sharpening: Sharpening is now halo-free and may look softer on edges where it used to create halos.
- Demosaicing: Fine detail will look cleaner, with less false color and moiré.
Your edits and slider values are not changed. Only the way they are rendered has changed.

Download Tethering Builds & Setup Guide (macOS & Linux)
1. Install libgphoto2 on your machine
RapidRAW uses libgphoto2 to communicate directly with connected cameras over USB. Because the tethering binary links dynamically against this library to stream live view and control camera settings, the driver must be present on your system for the app to detect and control your camera.
- macOS (via Homebrew):
  brew install libgphoto2 pkg-config
- Ubuntu / Debian:
  sudo apt update && sudo apt install -y libgphoto2-dev pkg-config
- Arch Linux:
  sudo pacman -S libgphoto2 pkgconf
- Fedora:
  sudo dnf install libgphoto2-devel pkgconf-pkg-config

This release is the result of a one-week sprint focused on making the core of RapidRAW faster and lighter on RAM. I rewrote large parts of the image pipeline, so thumbnails, previews, exports and batch actions are now much faster and use a lot less memory. On top of that, this update brings a full Immich integration with edits synced across all your computers, GPU acceleration for AI models, smart AI masks that adapt to every photo, new sky and foreground models, AI Text and Face masks, a rewritten dehaze and noise reduction, more accurate RAW colors and a new job queue.
New Features
Performance Improvements & Lower RAM Usage
This release is all about speed. I went through the whole app to find out where time and memory were wasted and rewrote large parts of the image pipeline:
- Faster Library: Thumbnails load much faster and scrolling through big folders feels smoother.
- Faster Editing: Previews update quicker while moving sliders, and preset previews render much faster.
- Faster Exports: Exports finish noticeably faster and use less RAM. Two new Advanced settings let you choose how many images are exported at the same time and how much free RAM a batch export may use.
- Faster Batch Actions: Pasting adjustments, resetting and auto lens correction across many images are now much quicker.
- Optimized GPU Shaders: The shaders were optimized and the histogram and scopes now run on a zero-copy pipeline, so they update without slowing down the editor.
- Smarter Decoding: Images that are already decoded are reused, for example in the culling view, the collage tool and tethering.
- Lower Memory Usage: RAM usage was reduced across the whole app, from the preview pipeline, masks and AI denoise to the UI itself.
Immich Integration
RapidRAW can now connect directly to your Immich server. A new Immich section in the library lets you browse your albums and timeline, and edit any photo just like a local file. Images show Immich's preview as a thumbnail and the original is only downloaded when you open or export it, so you don't need to sync your whole library to your computer.
The best part: your edits are stored together with the photo on your Immich server. This means your edits look the same on every computer and they are kept even if you clear your cache. If you edit the same photo on two computers, nothing gets lost: your local edits stay and the other version is kept as a virtual copy.
What you can do:
- Browse Albums & Timeline: Navigate your whole Immich library right inside RapidRAW. Large albums load fast, and stacks are shown once and open the RAW file.
- Synced Edits & Ratings: Changes are sent to Immich every few seconds and when you close the app. If the server is offline, RapidRAW shows how many edits are still waiting and sends them as soon as the server is back, even after a restart.
- Export to Immich: Immich is now a destination in the export panel. Your export is uploaded, stacked on top of its original and added to an album of your choice. This also works for photos from your local folders.
- Manage Your Library: Remove images from Immich albums, delete them to Immich's trash (where they can be restored for 30 days), or copy them to your local folders with their edits.
- Secure by Default: Your API key is stored in your system's credential store (Windows Credential Manager, macOS Keychain, Secret Service or Android Keystore).
Immich 2.5 or newer is required, as it is the first version that lets apps store their own data with a photo. Huge thanks to @cl1x for building this whole integration!
image
New Before / After Compare Modes
Comparing your edit with the original is now much more flexible. Next to the full original view, you can now choose split left/right, split top/bottom and side by side. Just right-click the compare button to choose a mode, or press B to toggle. In split mode, you can drag the divider to any position, and your zoom and position are kept when switching modes, so you can easily compare small details.
image
Smart AI Masks for Copy & Paste and Presets
Until now, when you copied a mask or saved it in a preset, AI masks kept the exact mask of the original photo. A pasted sky mask still showed the sky of the first image, which made AI masks pretty useless for batch editing.
Now, AI masks adapt to every photo. When you paste adjustments or apply a preset that contains AI masks, RapidRAW automatically generates them again for each image in the background: a sky mask finds the sky, a subject mask finds the subject and a face mask finds the face in every single photo. The same works for depth & normal maps and AI denoise. Lens Blur, Fog, Relight and AI Denoise are also new groups in the copy & paste dialog.
This makes it super easy to edit a whole shoot with local adjustments, without opening every image one by one.
Job Queue
Everything that runs in the background now shows up in one place. The new job queue replaces the old AI queue and covers exports, imports, file transfers, AI model downloads, AI tagging and all other AI work. You can follow the progress of each job, cancel running exports, and jump to your files with one click when a job is done. AI processing can be paused, resumed or retried, and pending AI work continues where it stopped after a restart.
image
Non-Destructive Batch Denoise & Classic Denoise
In v1.6.6, I promised GPU acceleration and non-destructive batch denoising for AI Denoise. Both are now here. AI Denoise runs on your GPU on Windows and macOS, and you can simply paste your denoise settings onto as many photos as you like. The job queue denoises them in the background, without creating a single extra file.
The old denoise modal, which saved a separate TIFF file, is now completely gone. For photographers who use AI-Free Mode, the Details panel now offers a non-destructive Classic Denoise based on BM3D instead.
Data Management & Storage
The Data Management section in the settings has been redesigned into a clear Storage page. You can now see exactly how much space RapidRAW uses on your device, split into thumbnails, metadata, AI models, AI denoise results, depth & normal maps, Immich downloads and logs. Each one can be cleared on its own, and you can set size limits for thumbnails, AI denoise, depth & normal maps and Immich downloads. Once a limit is reached, the least recently used files are removed automatically. Tools for clearing tags and edits from your library are also on this page.
image
New AI Sky & Foreground Models
The old U2Net models for sky and foreground masks have been replaced with EfficientSAM3 for the sky and BiRefNet for the foreground. The masks are now much more accurate, follow fine details like hair, branches and thin structures, and have cleaner edges. AI models are now also downloaded only when you first use a feature, so you don't need to download everything at once.

New Mask Types: AI Text Mask & Face Segmentation
There are two new AI mask types:
AI Text Mask
Simply type what you want to select, for example "person", "car" or "water", and RapidRAW creates a mask for it. This makes it super fast to select objects that are hard to paint by hand.
AI Text Mask
Face Segmentation
The new face mask finds the faces in your photo and lets you pick exactly which parts you want to edit on a small face illustration: face skin, body skin, hair, eyebrows, eye whites, iris & pupil, nose, lips and teeth. This is perfect for portrait retouching, like whitening teeth, brightening eyes or smoothing skin, without painting a single stroke.
Face Segmentation
GPU Acceleration for AI Models
The built-in AI features now run on your graphics card: denoise, masks, depth & normal maps and AI tagging. On Windows this uses DirectML with your high-performance GPU, and on macOS it uses CoreML. If your GPU is not supported, RapidRAW falls back to the CPU automatically, and you can turn GPU acceleration off in the settings if you ever run into problems.
image
Auto Adjust Levels
Auto adjust now comes with three strength levels: Subtle, Normal and Strong. Just right-click the Auto button in the editor, or pick a level from the right-click menu in the library to apply it to many photos at once. Auto adjust also no longer touches the Brightness slider and only sets the exposure, so your results are cleaner and easier to fine-tune.
image
Color-Preserving Highlight Reconstruction
Highlight recovery got another upgrade. RapidRAW now works directly on the RAW data and finds the real clipping point of each color channel in your photo. Areas where all channels are blown out are rebuilt with color from the surrounding pixels, so clipped areas keep their natural color, while bright light sources like lamps and the sun stay neutral instead of turning pink or yellow.

image image
More Accurate RAW Colors
RAW colors are now much more accurate, especially under artificial light:
- Dual-Illuminant Camera Color: Most cameras store two color profiles, one for daylight and one for warm tungsten light. RapidRAW now blends between them based on the white balance of your photo, just like the DNG standard does. Photos taken under tungsten or stage lights no longer get a magenta or purple cast.
- Gamut Compression: Very saturated colors that the camera can capture but sRGB can't show used to be hard clipped. They are now gently compressed instead, so strong stage lights and neon signs no longer turn into noisy blotches.
Rewritten Noise Reduction & Sharpening
I rewrote the manual noise reduction and sharpening in the main shader, together with the color noise reduction and sharpening that run when a RAW file is first loaded. Noise is now removed more cleanly while fine details stay crisp, and curved edges no longer show jagged artifacts.
image
Rewritten Dehaze

I am excited to bring you a new update that is all about image quality, precision color science, and complete workflow freedom. This release tackles core photography fundamentals from the ground up, introducing a camera-accurate Kelvin white balance engine with interactive area sampling alongside an edge-aware guided filter architecture. By replacing conventional blurs with this smarter system, adjustments like clarity, shadows, highlights, and a completely re-engineered whites slider now preserve delicate micro-textures without ever creating unnatural halos around high-contrast edges.
Beyond raw rendering quality, this update brings massive quality-of-life upgrades to your daily editing routine. You can now cull shoots in record time using dedicated Pick and Reject flags, tailor the sidebar to your exact habits with fully reorderable and collapsible panels, and take advantage of Apple’s Neural Engine-powered RAW 9 decoder on macOS. I'm also introducing RapidRAW Cloud for effortless, remote GPU generative cleanups without local hardware demands, balanced by a one-click AI-Free Mode for photographers who want a purely traditional, distraction-free editing workspace.
New Features
Kelvin White Balance with Area Sampling
This update completely overhauls how the app handles color temperature, turning white balance into a precise, camera-grade tool. In earlier versions, adjusting temperature and tint relied on rough guesswork sliders and a basic eyedropper that merely sampled a single screen pixel, often leading to uneven or unnatural color shifts.
RapidRAW now reads the white balance recorded by your camera in RAW files and lets you toggle into true Kelvin temperatures, ensuring that light adjustments behave just like real-world daylight or warm indoor lamps.
image
Alongside this, the eyedropper tool has been completely redesigned: as you move across the canvas, a floating preview card displays live color readings, and you can now click and drag a box over any neutral gray or white area to smooth out image noise and calculate the correct balance automatically. Together, these changes make neutralizing unwanted color casts and dialing in the perfect photographic mood both effortless and true to life.
image
Guided Filter for Edge-Aware Adjustments
Fine detail enhancements no longer produce distracting halos. In place of standard blurs, clarity, structure, dehaze, shadows, and highlights now run through an edge-aware filtering system that cleanly separates broad lighting changes from sharp object contours. When lifting dark shadows or taming highlights, the software captures original surface micro-textures and feeds them back into the picture. Textures like skin, fabric, and foliage stay crisp and authentic rather than muddying together.

Rewritten Whites Slider
Previously, the whites slider simply boosted areas with a flat multiplier, which easily blew out highlights and erased delicate textures. Now, it applies a smooth, targeted curve that brightens the lightest tones while directly reinjecting fine surface details and mid-level textures back in. As a result, bright areas like clouds, snow, or white clothing gain extra brilliance and pop without turning into flat, featureless patches.
Pick and Reject Flags
Culling large shoots is now significantly faster thanks to a dedicated flagging workflow. You can mark favorites as "Picked" or bad takes as "Rejected" using quick keyboard shortcuts, visual badges, or bottom bar toggles. Rejected photos automatically dim in your library, making it easy to filter them out of view or delete all of them at once with a single confirmation.
image
Apple RAW 9 Decoding and Denoising Support
Mac users can now tap directly into Apple’s advanced RAW 9 engine. Designed to take full advantage of the Neural Engine, this system demosaics camera sensor data and cleans up image noise in a single unified step. You can enable this engine in the RapidRAW processing settings as your default RAW developer, or pick it inside the Denoise menu. Unsupported cameras or file types seamlessly fall back to the built-in processor without interrupting your workflow.
RapidRAW Cloud Integration
RapidRAW is built on the belief that great photo editing should never be locked behind a paywall. The entire editor, its full RAW processing engine, smart masking, and built-in spot removal tools remain 100% free and run privately right on your own computer. If you have a dedicated graphics card and enjoy managing your own setup, you can even connect your own local server to run advanced generative tasks without paying a single cent. You have total freedom over how you edit, and nothing you already use is being restricted or hidden away.
image
For those who simply want effortless object removal without buying an expensive graphics card or wrestling with technical installations, RapidRAW Cloud is here purely as a convenience. With a quick sign-in, remote servers handle the heavy lifting for complex textures and large removals - only processing the small patch you brush over and deleting it immediately, so your full RAW files never leave your computer. At $14 a month, it is an easy, zero-hassle upgrade that gives you remote editing when you want it, while directly funding independent, open-source development without venture capital, bloat, or ads.
As this is the initial rollout of RapidRAW Cloud, your early feedback is crucial! Whether it's processing speed, inpainting quality, or workflow suggestions, please share your thoughts via GitHub, Email or Discord so I can continue refining the experience.
Learn more at: https://www.getrapidraw.com/cloud
image
AI-Free Mode
For photographers who prefer a purely traditional workflow or need to follow strict photo contest rules, RapidRAW includes a dedicated AI-Free Mode. Flipping this single switch completely hides all generative buttons, AI masks, and neural tools, automatically reverting features like noise reduction back to classic algorithms. Your existing edits will still display normally, leaving you with a clean, distraction-free workspace focused entirely on authentic photography.
image
Reorderable and Collapsible Adjustment Panels
Your editing workspace is now completely modular. You can drag and drop to reorder entire sections and individual tools, hide controls you rarely touch, and collapse items to save vertical space. The app automatically remembers your preferred arrangement and open sections, keeping your workspace clean, organized, and tailored to how you work.
image
Savable Custom Aspect Ratios
You can now save your favorite custom crop aspect ratios as permanent presets. After typing in any unique width and height, clicking the save icon adds it directly alongside your standard crop buttons with an automatically formatted label. These custom ratios stay saved across all your editing sessions, and you can remove them anytime with a single click.
Core Improvements
- Precision Curves: Added a fine adjust mode for tone curves, plus inactive channels now show as colored overlay curves and reference markers.
- Crop Enhancements: Center-anchor crop resizing by holding Ctrl/Cmd, and align framing with a new center mark guide.
- Export Options: Added borders and aspect ratio padding to exports, embedded sRGB ICC profiles, and refreshed export presets.
- AI Task Controls: Added real-time progress tracking in the UI with the ability to cancel running AI tasks.
- Interface Polish: Streamlined adjustment panel customization and improved default tool visibility across the workspace.
- Metadata & Color Fixes: Improved lens EXIF detection and refined continuous RAW magenta highlight corrections.
- Localization: Added full Dutch & Netherlands language support.
- Stability & Bug Fixes: Resolved various issues and refined overall application performance.
Community & Acknowledgments
A huge amount of community effort went into making this release possible. While I was away on a one-week road trip through Austria, several amazing contributors stepped up to keep the momentum going, with a special shoutout and massive thank you to @lalibertemarc for their exceptional help, dedication, and consistently high-quality contributions across this release cycle.
Note for Upgrading Users
Due to the introduction of the new camera-accurate Kelvin white balance engine and updated tint shaders, white balance handling has changed significantly. As a result, existing edits opened in v1.6.5 may appear slightly different, potentially shifting more magenta or greenish compared to previous versions as they map to the new, physically accurate color pipeline.
Recommendation: If you are in the middle of editing an active client shoot or critical project, I strongly recommend finishing and exporting your work on your current version before upgrading. Once your current shoot is wrapped up, upgrade to v1.6.5 to take full advantage of the improved color science for your next projects.
Thank you for your understanding!

RapidRAW has officially crossed 10,000 GitHub stars and over 610,000 downloads. What started as an empty project folder on my laptop has grown into an incredible global community of photographers and open-source contributors. To celebrate this milestone, I wrote a deep-dive reflection on the entire journey, covering the early prototypes, the late-night shader experiments, and the path forward. You can read the full retrospective on the blog.
Alongside this milestone, version 1.6.4 delivers one of the most technically challenging updates yet: rebuilt highlight recovery capable of reconstructing clipped color channels. This release also reworks the shader pipeline to introduce true exposure adjustments, adds a responsive masonry grid layout to the library, includes faster crop and pan canvas shortcuts, offers a neutral grey canvas mode, and squashes several backend bugs across export and EXIF handling.
New Features
Highlight Recovery
To be 100% honest with you: highlight recovery was always one of the weaker spots in RapidRAW. I spent so many hours trying to get it right in the past that I started telling myself it was just "too hard" to solve nicely. But over the last few days, I had a strong urge to finally crack it, and I'm honestly blown away by how well it works now. RapidRAW can now reconstruct clipped highlights (> 1.0) using the remaining color channel information.

Alongside this, I reworked parts of the shader pipeline. To reflect how the math actually works now:
- The Exposure slider (previously EV Shift) is now a true Exposure slider that cleanly pulls down overexposed highlights.
- The old exposure slider has been renamed to Brightness. It runs after the tonemapper, letting you tweak perceived image brightness without introducing clipping.
New Crop, Pan & Zoom Shortcuts
It might seem like a small detail, but this is a massive workflow improvement. You no longer have to open the crop tool and drag the corner handles every single time:

RapidRAW v1.6.2 brings major new capabilities to your creative workflow. This release adds native Camera Tethering for remote studio shooting, an intelligent Focus Stacking engine, built-in Analog Film Emulations in a scene-referred color pipeline, and a rewritten deconvolution-based sharpening engine alongside numerous stability and usability fixes.
New Features
Focus Stacking
RapidRAW now includes an intelligent Focus Stacking tool alongside the panorama stitcher and HDR merge features. Focus stacking lets you combine multiple exposures captured at varying focus distances into a single image with incredible front-to-back sharpness and extended depth of field. This is essential for macro, product, and landscape photography, where physical optical limits prevent keeping the entire scene in focus.

Camera Tethering (macOS & Linux)
RapidRAW now supports native Camera Tethering for studio, portrait, and product photography workflows. Connect your camera over USB to shoot directly into your workspace.
tethering
What you can do:
- Real-time Live View: Stream live view with composition guide overlays, 90° rotation, and horizontal flipping.
- Camera Controls: Adjust Shutter Speed, Aperture, ISO, White Balance, and more directly from the sidebar.
- Automatic Color Grading: Automatically apply a chosen preset to incoming shots the moment they are captured.
- Ghost Overlay: Overlay your previous shot on top of the live view to keep framing and perspective consistent across shots.
- Instant Ingestion: Captured photos automatically save into your current library folder and can open straight in the editor.
Important: System Requirements & Dedicated Builds
Because tethering relies on the system library libgphoto2, it is provided as a separate build (_tethering) for macOS and Linux.
To use tethering, you must install libgphoto2 on your system first, then download the corresponding _tethering package from the tethering release downloads table below.
Built-in Analog Film Emulations
RapidRAW now comes with built-in, scientifically modeled analog film emulations out of the box, powered by the open-source spektrafilm project by Andrea Volpato.
image
Highlights & Color Pipeline:
- True Scene-Referred Pipeline: Unlike standard display-space LUTs that clip highlights and crush shadows, these emulations run in a scene-referred V-Log color pipeline directly inside the GPU shader. This ensures natural highlight roll-off, rich organic color response, and deep tonal transitions.
- Non-Destructive & Adjustable: Fine-tune the look with the intensity slider, combine it with tone curves, or stack it with film grain and halation for an authentic analog aesthetic.
Special thanks to Andrea Volpato for creating spektrafilm and making these spectrally accurate film profiles available under the CC BY-SA 4.0 license.
Rewritten Sharpening Algorithm
The sharpening tool now uses a multi-scale deconvolution algorithm with built-in halo suppression and directional edge smoothing. It enhances fine micro-details cleanly across the frame without creating harsh ringing artifacts or amplifying shadow noise.
Drag & Drop Image Move System
You can now easily organize your library by selecting multiple images and dragging them directly into folders or albums.
image Core Improvements
- Full EXIF Metadata Preservation on Export: Exported images now preserve and embed full camera capture and EXIF metadata.
- Tablet & Touch Interface Restoration: Restored side panel layouts and controls on tablet and touch screen devices.
- Inpainting Auto-Cropping: Added automatic canvas cropping for generative AI inpainting workflows.
- Stability & Bug Fixes: Resolved various issues and refined overall application performance.

This update brings a boost in rendering speed, a reworked preset system, and the first steps onto Android. I've built a direct WGPU renderer that skips the usual webview overhead, making the app feel incredibly fast. I've also rewritten the presets system so you can now create "Tool" presets that stack on top of your edits, and you can finally save masks and crops into them. On top of that, there's a new mask intersect mode alongside new flow masks, and several highly requested workflow improvements like batch denoising or keeping EXIF data for stitched and denoised files.
New Features
Direct WGPU Renderer
I've implemented a direct WGPU renderer that bypasses Tauri's standard communication and browser decoding. It essentially draws a native window behind the webview, making the editing experience noticeably smoother.
Note for especially Linux users: This new renderer is currently experimental and not available on Linux. Tauri uses GTK for webviews on Linux, which conflicts with WGPU on the same screen surface and causes flickering. To keep things stable, Linux versions will safely default to the standard webview renderer for now. For more informations, check this issue: tauri-apps/tauri#9220.
Reworked Presets System
The presets system has been completely rebuilt to give you more flexibility in your workflow.
- Style vs. Tool Presets: You can now set a preset to be a "Style" (which overwrites the entire image's settings) or a "Tool" (which acts additively, blending new changes on top of your current edit).
- Mask & Crop Support: You can now save your masks and crops directly into your presets.
image
Experimental Android Support
I'm excited to officially bring RapidRAW to Android! This is an early, experimental build, so you might run into a few bugs. Currently, the UI is specifically optimized for tablets (it will not display properly on phones yet). General editing and masking are working nicely.
The AI tools require a lot of memory, so I highly recommend testing this on an Android device with at least 8 GB of RAM.
Many thanks to @Duecki1 for the support in releasing RapidRAW for Android.
Intersecting Masks
You can now easily intersect masks, making complex masking workflows simpler and more precise.
image
Flow Masks
The new Flow Mask type works like an additive brush. It builds up strength when you paint over the same area multiple times, which is perfect for dodge and burn adjustments.
image
Copy/Paste Upgrades
You can now copy and paste masks and crops between images! This is turned off by default to prevent accidental overwrites, but you can easily enable it in the copy/paste settings.
image
Fluid Canvas Navigation
I've completely rewritten the engine for zooming, panning, and pinching on the canvas. Trackpad users on macOS will notice it finally feels completely native and smooth.
Windows users: There is currently a minor gesture quirk on Windows, so you will need to hold down CTRL while using a two-finger scroll to zoom. A more seamless fix is planned for a future update!
Retaining EXIF Data
Denoised and stitched images now keep their original EXIF data (saved using the new .rrexif format). This means you will no longer lose your lens correction profiles, capture dates, or export data when running these intensive processes.
Core Improvements
- Better Auto-Adjust: The auto-adjustment algorithm has been greatly improved to deliver faster, more accurate results.
- Redesigned Color Wheels: The color grading wheels have been redesigned for a clean, consistent look and now feature dynamic sliders.
- Batch Processing Upgrades: I've added batch denoising and a new option to preserve your exact folder structure when exporting in batches.
- AVIF Export: Added support for AVIF export.
- Removed mask limits.
- Improved the downscaling algorithm so you feel less of a difference when dragging sliders.
- Fixed bugs that occurred when rapidly switching between images.
- General UI polish, bug fixes & usability improvements.

This update is packed with new editing tools and smarter processing. I've added AI-powered denoising based on nind-denoise, a full image analytics panel with waveforms and scopes, and new parametric masking options for targeting specific colors or luminance zones. Subject masking has also been upgraded with SAM-2 models and single-click selection. On the export side, there's now support for JPEG XL, WebP, and CUBE LUTs - the last one being great if you want to bring color grades from RapidRAW into a video editor. Under the hood, I've added an LRU cache for instant image switching and region-of-interest rendering, which makes editing while zoomed in significantly faster.
New Features
NIND Denoising
Previously, RapidRAW only had a traditional BM3D denoiser. It produced decent results, but it was never really competitive with the newer AI-based denoising methods found in other software.
So I'm excited to introduce a new denoising method based on nind-denoise. It can be applied directly to RAW images to naturally remove noise while preserving detail.
The results speak for themselves:
───────────────┬───────────┬───────────
Original       │BM3D       │NIND
───────────────┼───────────┼───────────
Original       │BM3D       │NIND
───────────────┴───────────┴───────────
Due to dependency limitations, NIND denoise is not yet GPU accelerated, so it will take some time to process each image. In future versions, once things have matured, I plan to support batch denoising and move the processing over to the RapidRAW AI Connector, which supports GPU acceleration.
Credits for this denoising method go to @trougnouf's nind-denoise.
Image Analytics Panel
RapidRAW now features a switchable image analytics panel, giving you multiple ways to exactly visualize what's going on with your edit in real time.
Supported modes:
- Luma Waveform
- RGB Waveform
- RGB Parade
- Vectorscope
- RGB Histogram
Parametric Color & Luminance Masks
I've added two new mask types that let you quickly target specific color ranges or luminance zones in your image.
Parametric Masks
Single Point Subject Masks
This release ships with updated, more accurate, and higher resolution AI subject detection models based on SAM-2. On top of that, I've implemented single point masking - just click on your subject and it gets selected. No need to draw a bounding box around it first.
Single Point Subject Mask
JPEG XL, WebP, and Additional Format Support
This update adds support for a bunch of new export formats, including JPEG XL, WebP, and CUBE LUTs. The LUT export is something I'm particularly happy about: You can screenshot a frame from your video editor, color grade it in RapidRAW, export the result as a LUT, and then apply that same color grade back in the video editor at full quality.
Export formats
LRU Cache
RapidRAW now keeps recently viewed images in a cache, so switching between them is instant and seamless. This is especially useful when you're culling and need to quickly flip back and forth to check focus.
ROI Rendering
Previously, dragging sliders while zoomed in would lag and stutter because the entire image was being reprocessed on every change. Now RapidRAW only processes the region that's actually visible in the viewport, which gives a huge speedup when editing zoomed in.
Core Improvements
- Improved tonemapper & shader, particularly how it behaves within masked regions
- Refined keybinds across the app for a smoother editing workflow
- Various UI polish and visual tweaks
- A ton of bug fixes under the hood - too many to list individually ;)

- Whole Image Mask Type: Added a new mask type that covers the entire image, useful as a base for subtracting or inverting other mask components. This also lays the groundwork for future mask types without cluttering the UI.

Core Improvements
- Library thumbnail updating is now much smoother.
- Rawler is now a submodule, thanks to @william-sy.
- The logger has been improved to output the full traceback for better debugging.

Performance Hotfix
Version 1.4.1 addresses critical performance issues introduced in v1.4.0, where using local contrast tools could cause severe slowdowns and even crashes.
I strongly recommend skipping v1.4.0 and upgrading directly to v1.4.1.

Important: Action Required for Upgrading Users
In this update, I've had to change the application's internal identifier from com.rapidraw.app to io.github.CyberTimon.RapidRAW. This is a technical but important change that helps with long-term maintenance and ensures better compatibility going forward.
Unfortunately, this means that when you first launch v1.4.0, it won't be able to find your existing user data. As a result:
- Your AI models will need to be redownloaded.
- Your library thumbnails will be regenerated.
- Crucially, all of your saved presets will be gone.
- Edits aren't effected, as they are stored in seperate sidecars.
To avoid losing your data, I've outlined two migration options below. Please choose one before you launch the new version for the first time. Keep in mind that edits are stored in sidecars and aren't affected by this migration.
Option A: Full Migration (Recommended)
This method is the best option as it migrates everything: your settings, presets, and cached data. To do this, you'll need to manually rename the application's data folder.
- Windows: Navigate to both %APPDATA% (in Roaming) and %LOCALAPPDATA% (in Local) and rename the com.rapidraw.app folder in each location to io.github.CyberTimon.RapidRAW.
- macOS: Navigate to ~/Library/Application Support/ and rename the com.rapidraw.app folder to io.github.CyberTimon.RapidRAW. Example command: mv ~/Library/Application\ Support/com.rapidraw.app ~/Library/Application\ Support/io.github.CyberTimon.RapidRAW
- Linux: The location can vary, but typically check ~/.config/ and ~/.local/share/. Rename the com.rapidraw.app folder in each relevant location to io.github.CyberTimon.RapidRAW.
Option B: Migrate Presets Only
If you only care about saving your presets and don't mind re-caching thumbnails and models, this is a simpler alternative.
1. In your old version of RapidRAW, export all your presets to a safe location.
2. Install and open RapidRAW v1.4.0.
3. Import your presets using the new Universal Preset Importer.
I sincerely apologize for the inconvenience this one-time migration step causes. This change was a tough decision, but it sets the app up for a more stable and robust future. Thank you for your understanding!

Running on macOS and Windows
Because RapidRAW is not yet code-signed, both macOS and Windows may show warnings when you try to run the app.
- On macOS:
  You’ll need to remove the quarantine flag after installation:
  xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/RapidRAW.app
  Without this step, macOS may report the app as "corrupted."
- On Windows:
  When launching the app, you may see a Windows Defender SmartScreen warning.
  - Click "More info" → "Run anyway" to continue.

Generative AI Improvements

Optimised Image Editing
One of the biggest bottlenecks in RapidRAW used to be the slow base64 bridge between the backend and frontend. Encoding/decoding large images added a ton of overhead when applying adjustments or just opening files.
That’s now fixed. I switched over to Tauri’s IPC response, which avoids the whole base64 step. The result: editing feels way smoother, and fullscreen zoom actually loads the full res image so you can check every pixel.
